title: Mister Donut Returns to China for First Time Since 2019
paragraphs: The Japanese doughnut chain Mister Donut has returned to mainland China, about seven years after it left the country.

At the end of September, Duskin, the Japanese company that runs Mister Donut, opened a new store in a busy shopping mall in Shanghai. The store is a takeaway shop, which means customers buy their doughnuts and take them away instead of eating inside.

The new store sells many of Mister Donut's traditional favorites from its menu in Japan. It also offers special items that are only available in China, such as banana-flavored doughnuts, which are popular with local customers.

According to a Chinese business report, the company has signed a franchise agreement with a company in Shanghai. Under the agreement, the brand can open stores in Shanghai and in the provinces of Zhejiang, Jiangsu and Shandong. The report said Mister Donut plans to open five stores by the end of the year.
The company has not said exactly where these other stores will be or when each of them will open.

This is not the first time Mister Donut has been in China. The chain first opened stores in the country in 1999, but it left in 2019 after about 20 years. At the time, reports said the business was losing money. Some reports also said that Chinese customers were choosing foods with more local flavors, as well as healthier foods.

Before returning to mainland China, Mister Donut had already started to grow in other parts of the region. In 2024, the chain opened its first store in Hong Kong, at the K11 Art Mall in Tsim Sha Tsui. It said it planned to have nine stores in Hong Kong by 2027.
Now, with its new store in Shanghai, the company is hoping that Chinese customers will give its doughnuts a second chance.
